proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (V6, representation of Γ); the lower density hypothesis is supplied there by lower_density and the null-set clause by (REP).
1. Dual norm. For an n-vector ζ put |ζ|* := sup{ζ(β) : |β| ≤ 1}. The space of n-covectors is finite dimensional and covectorEuclideanNorm is a norm on it (if all coefficients α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n}), i_1 < ⋯ < i_n, vanish then α = 0 by multilinearity and alternation), so its closed unit ball is compact and the supremum is attained; |·|* is a norm on Λ_n (hence continuous), |ζ(α)| ≤ |ζ|*|α|, and |ζ|* ≤ 1 iff |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. (If n > P all n-covectors vanish, Λ_n = 0, Γ = 0, μ = 0 and M := ∅ works.)
2. |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e. x ↦ |ξ(x)|* is μ-a.e. measurable with values in [0, 1]. For ω admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 everywhere), Γ(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ ≤ ∫|ξ(x)|*|ω(x)|dμ ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ. Hence μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, so ∫(1 − |ξ|*)dμ = 0 with 1 − |ξ|* ≥ 0, i.e. |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e.
3. Borel normalized field. Choose ξ₀ strongly measurable with ξ = ξ₀ μ-a.e. and set ζ(x) := ξ₀(x)/max(1, |ξ₀(x)|*). ζ is strongly measurable (continuous function of ξ₀), |ζ(x)|* ≤ 1, i.e. |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and ζ = ξ₀ wherever |ξ₀|* ≤ 1, in particular wherever ξ₀ = ξ: ζ = ξ μ-a.e. Hence Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ for all ω and |ζ|* = 1 μ-a.e.
4. The density set. Θ(x) := liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ). S := {x : Θ(x) < η₀} is μ-null; let N₁ := toMeasurable μ S (a Borel superset with μ(N₁) = 0) and M₀ := ℝ^P∖N₁: Borel, μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0 and Θ ≥ η₀ on M₀. (Alternatively Θ is Borel, as in the parent: x ↦ μ(B_r(x)) is lower semicontinuous and r ↦ μ(B_r(x)) left continuous, so the liminf may be taken over rational radii.)
5. Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞ (Vitali covering; a non-sharp constant suffices). For x ∈ M₀ and all small ρ > 0, μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nρⁿ. Fix δ > 0 and let 𝓑 be the family of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ M₀, 0 < ρ < δ and μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nρⁿ; it covers M₀ finely. By the Vitali 5r-covering lemma (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall; Simon Ch. 1, 3.4) there is a disjoint subfamily (B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i))_{i∈I} with M₀ ⊆ ⋃_iB̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i); I is countable (ℝ^P is separable; disjoint balls with non-empty interior). Then Σ_i(10ρ_i)ⁿ ≤ (2·10ⁿ/(η₀ω_n))Σ_iμ(B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i)) ≤ 2·10ⁿμ(ℝ^P)/(η₀ω_n) =: Λ < ∞, and diam B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i) ≤ 10δ. By the definition of μH[n] (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum along δ → 0), μH[n](M₀) ≤ Λ, hence Hⁿ(M₀) = c_n·μH[n](M₀) < ∞ with the finite constant c_n of euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def.
6. Radon–Nikodym. ν₀ := Hⁿ⌞M₀ is finite and μ ≪ ν₀: if Hⁿ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 then μ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 by hypothesis and μ(E∖M₀) ≤ μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0 (for non-measurable E use a measurable superset). By the Lebesgue decomposition μ = μ.singularPart ν₀ + ν₀.withDensity(μ.rnDeriv ν₀) (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add) and μ.singularPart ν₀ = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac), so μ = ν₀.withDensity h with h := μ.rnDeriv ν₀ measurable [0, ∞]-valued, h < ∞ ν₀-a.e. (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top), ∫_{M₀}h dHⁿ = μ(ℝ^P) < ∞.
7. The carrier. M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} ∩ {|ζ|* = 1}, Borel. μ(ℝ^P∖M) = 0: μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0; μ(M₀ ∩ {h = 0}) = ∫_{M₀∩{h=0}}h dHⁿ = 0; ν₀{h = ∞} = 0 hence μ{h = ∞} = 0; μ{|ζ|* ≠ 1} = 0 (step 3). Hⁿ(M) ≤ Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞. Put θ := (1_M·h).toReal: Borel, θ > 0 on M and ofReal(θ(x)) = h(x) for x ∈ M.
8. μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ): for Borel E, μ(E) = μ(E ∩ M) = ∫_{E∩M}h d(Hⁿ⌞M₀) = ∫_{E∩M}ofReal(θ)dHⁿ (M ⊆ M₀).
9. Representation. Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ(ω)d((Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ)) = ∫_M(ofReal θ).toReal·ζ(ω)dHⁿ = ∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ(x) (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul; (ofReal θ).toReal = θ as θ ≥ 0).
10. Pointwise properties on M: θ > 0 (step 7); |ζ(x)|* = 1, so by step 1 some β with |β| ≤ 1 has ζ(x)(β) = 1; |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| everywhere (step 3); Θ(x) ≥ η₀ (M ⊆ M₀, step 4). With Hⁿ(M) < ∞, θ Borel and ζ strongly measurable, all assertions hold. ∎
key_steps: |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e. because μ(ℝ^P) = M(Γ) ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ; replace ξ by a Borel normalized ζ.
M₀ := complement of a Borel μ-null set containing {Θ < η₀}; a Vitali 5r-covering gives Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞.
μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M₀; Lebesgue decomposition gives the density h; carrier M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} ∩ {|ζ|* = 1}, θ := h.toReal.
Transfer Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ to Γ(ω) = ∫_Mθζ(ω)dHⁿ and read off the pointwise properties on M.
